Work Orders was open in three browser tabs as the same user.
Tab A was switched to Tech View, then a few seconds later tab B was switched to Board View.
After refreshing, tab A and tab B both opened in Board View, and a new tab C also opened in Board View: the last choice made.
No warning or conflict message appeared in any tab.

Board View was chosen at full width.

Back at full width the display switcher was offered again (List, Tech View, Board View) and the page was in Board View: the narrow window did not change the saved choice.
Tablet held sideways not checked (optional). Edge not checked by hand.

doubt.C96920: Same as before, now on a settled staging site: with the network off, clicking Tech View did not switch the display; the Work Orders area was replaced by "Something went wrong loading this section" with Retry, and "Part of the page failed to load. Your connection may have dropped.". The other two points held: after reconnecting the page opened in Board View, and Tech View chosen online was kept. Why I do not call it Failed: the part of the screen that draws Tech View had to be downloaded at that moment because this fresh browser had never opened Tech View. A tester whose browser has opened Tech View before may well have it stored. The QA lead should decide whether the case expects Tech View to work offline in a browser that has never opened it, or re-run after opening Tech View once before going offline.
doubt.C96973: With Assigned to me on, only my own column (Admin ShopView, 1) was shown. The Reassign dialog offered Ralph Edwards and Jenny Wilson although their columns were not on screen. After picking Ralph Edwards: "Lead technician updated", and the work order disappeared from the board without a reload. The doubt: instead of my column staying with a count of 0, as the case words it ("your column count goes from 1 to 0"), the whole board switched to "No work orders match these filters / Try removing a filter to widen your results / Clear all filters" with no columns. Other cases say other rules apply when nothing matches the filters, so this may be correct. The QA lead should decide whether the empty-results screen satisfies the case. Also, the case names Dana Ortiz as the second outside technician; the script checked Jenny Wilson. Second run: it stopped again on the same empty-results screen ("No work orders match these filters"), so nothing new was read.
